description_full: Turkcell Iletisim Hizmetleri A.S., together with its subsidiaries, engages in establishing and operating a global system for mobile communications (GSM) network in Turkey, Belarus, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Germany, and the Netherlands. It operates through the Turkcell Turkiye, Turkcell International, and Techfin segments. The company is involved in information technology, value added GSM, and entertainment investment, as well as research and development, digital and insurance agency, property investments, electricity energy trade, and wholesale and retail electricity sales activities. It also provides telecommunications, television, and content; digitalization; sales, delivery, and digital sales; consumer financing; cloud solutions; online radio, television, and on-demand streaming; telecommunications infrastructure; electronic payment; and develop software products and services. In addition, the company offers customer relations and human resources management; directory assistance; payment services and e-money; internet search engine and browser; venture capital investment fund; meal coupons and cards; data processing; data center and cloud; programming and technical support; and digital education services. Further, it provides training software developers. Turkcell Iletisim Hizmetleri A.S. was incorporated in 1993 and is headquartered in Istanbul, Turkey.

financial_summary: Turkcell Iletisim Hizmetleri AS is a mid-cap communication services business with a $4.0B market cap on $4.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 18% against a 10% cost of capital, a 7-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 30%.

The business throws off $1.2B in free cash flow — roughly 26 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.33× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -15.1% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.2× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 0.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.7% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 7% operating margin is roughly in line with the Communication Services median (9%).

mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 12% over the past year excluding the latest month.

val: The stock trades 90% below its DCF fair value of $45.94, a meaningful margin of safety.

Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 30.0% (above the risk-free rate).
The 2 covering analysts target $7.33 on average, 60% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 18% clears the cost of capital of 10.4% by 7pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.52).

hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.2x net debt to EBITDA ($1.7B of cash against $2.0B of debt), and interest cover is thin at 0.4x.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 3.6% over 3 years and 0.5% over 5 years, so growth is accelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 14.3% a year over five years.
Analysts expect 68.2% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.7%, and institutions hold 6%.
It returns 2.7% a year to shareholders (0.1% in buybacks and 2.4% in dividends).
